On this page

Modes & Permissions ​

Three independent dials control what an agent may do and how hard it thinks. They are easy to confuse, so this page separates them.

1. Delegation mode — ask vs work ​

Set per delegation and per checklist task.

ModeTool setWritesTypical use
askRead, Grep, GlobNeverInvestigation, code reading, answering a question about a repo
workFull (subject to agent permission)Yes — commits, and opens a PR under branch: newMaking the change

An ask cannot become a work mid-flight. If an investigation concludes that a change is needed, that is a new task with mode: 'work', which is exactly the moment the approval gate should see it.

2. Agent permission — all / read-only / custom ​

Set in AGENT.md frontmatter, or via Settings → Permissions. This is a property of the agent, not the delegation.

PermissionTools
allEvery tool (default)
read-onlyExactly ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob']
customExactly the tools: allow-list

Enforcement is two-layered: the SDK is constructed with the restricted tool set, and a canUseTool gate sits behind it. A read-only agent handed a work delegation is still read-only — the narrower of the two wins.

3. Effort mode ​

The reasoning tier for a call. It resolves most-specific-first:

task.effort
  → Run.agentConfigs[actor].effort
    → Run.effortMode
      → CustomAgent.effort
        → global default (Settings)

Per-task effort is what stops a plan from spending its heaviest tier on a file lookup and its cheapest on the hard implementation step. Spend enforcement may clamp the effort down when an allowance is running out, rather than refusing the call outright.

Project policy — the approval gate ​

Separate from all three, and it governs writes to a repo. Declared in memory/projects/<name>.md frontmatter:

KeyValuesDefault
branchnew (cut saidi/* + PR) | current (commit on the checked-out branch)new
approvalconfirm (ask before any write) | auto (proceed)confirm
verifyShell command run after a work delegation commitsnone

An unset, missing, or invalid value falls back to the built-in safe policy — new + confirm — unless the operator has changed the fallback in Settings → System. There is no permissive global default that silently applies.

Operator permissions (multi-member installs) ​

Beyond the agent dials, org members carry permission keys that gate what they may do — including run steering and visibility:

KeyGrants
runs.steerAllSteer any run, not just your own
runs.viewAllSee every run in the org

A run's owner can always steer it; a member it was sharedWith can watch the thread but not steer. Every turn and delegation in a run resolves budgets, permissions, and connections against the run's createdBy member.

Choosing sensibly ​

  • Start every new repo at approval: confirm and branch: new. Move to auto only for repos where a bad commit is cheap to discard.
  • Give a custom agent read-only unless it demonstrably needs to write. custom with a short allow-list beats all for anything touching an external system.
  • Set verify: on every repo that has a test command. It is the cheapest way to make "done" mean something.

See also: Project Policy · Guardrails
